summary.short: Requires the Information Commissioner to prepare a code of practice giving good-practice guidance on processing personal data when developing and using AI and automated decision-making under the UK GDPR and the Data Protection Act 2018 (except Part 4), including children's data. In force from 12 May 2026, UK-wide.
summary.long: These Regulations, made 16 April 2026 under sections 124A and 124B of the Data Protection Act 2018, require the Information Commissioner to prepare an appropriate code of practice. The code gives guidance on good practice in processing personal data under the relevant data protection legislation when developing and using artificial intelligence and when making automated decisions. It must also include guidance on processing children's personal data. Automated decision-making is defined by reference to Article 22C(1) of the UK GDPR and section 50C(1) of the 2018 Act. Relevant data protection legislation means the UK GDPR and the 2018 Act, except Part 4. Regulation 3 modifies section 124B so that the panel considering the code must not consider or report on any aspect of the code relating to national security. The Regulations come into force 21 days after being laid (stated as 12 May 2026) and extend to England and Wales, Scotland and Northern Ireland. The Explanatory Note states that no full impact assessment was produced for the instrument, and that the Commissioner must produce one when preparing the code.

relations.note: Regulation 3 applies section 124B to the preparation or amendment of the code as if a new subsection (7A) (no panel consideration of national security aspects) were inserted after subsection (7). This is a modification as applied, not a textual amendment of the 2018 Act.

relations.note: Regulation 2(3) defines automated decision-making by reference to decision-making to which Article 22C(1) of the UK GDPR applies. Regulation 2(3) also defines relevant data protection legislation to include the UK GDPR.

thresholds.note: The instrument contains no numeric cutoff that changes legal treatment. The only numbers are the commencement period in reg. 1(2) (21 days after laying), which is a procedural time limit and is coded as an event, not a threshold. Regulation 2 requires a code of practice but sets no thresholds. Regulation 3 modifies the section 124B panel requirements without numeric cutoffs.
